questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It reduces the effect of alcohol on your driving.
It has no effect on your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (including illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medications) harm your brain function and make driving unsafe. Mixing alcohol with drugs increases your crash risk.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: How do you help prevent a rear-end collision?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop. Release the gas pedal first to slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly with steady pressure to light up your brake lights and stop safely.

questions.question: What should you do when a car's bright headlights blind you?

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If another car has its high beams on, look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded while the car passes.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not crowd vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which lane should you turn into when turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while you are turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ends.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn you of upcoming hazards. This sign means the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Travels at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers get distracted. A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Stops distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: To have enough time to react to mistakes by other drivers, leave plenty of space between your vehicle and the vehicles around you.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs mean:

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You may go when the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians and it is safe to proceed.

questions.question: If another person is injured in an accident, you should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Avoid moving the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid moving the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary. Moving them the wrong way can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: Small children in a vehicle should:

options.text: Be safely held by a strong adult.
Stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Never ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Special car seats are needed for small children. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always secure children in proper seats.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare you for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Orange signs are:

options.text: Work zone signs.
Traffic law signs.
School zone signs.
Direction signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are diamond-shaped, orange, and have black letters or symbols. They warn that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when someone wants to pass you. This creates room in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Accelerate as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, you must first let pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection cross safely.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: If you are at fault in an accident and do not pay for damages:

options.text: Your driver license and/or plates will be suspended for one year.
You will save money.
Your car will be taken away.
You must buy a new car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driver license and/or plates will be suspended for one year.
questions.explanation: If you are at fault in an accident and do not pay for damages, your driver license and vehicle plates will be suspended for one year. You can get them back during that year if you pay a fee and show proof that you have paid for the damages.

questions.question: You see an oncoming car to the left and a bicyclist to the right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Split the difference.
Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you face multiple hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. What should you know?

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians are responsible to stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided. This shape is used only for stop signs. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?

options.text: Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.
Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
Can disregard any pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Wait for all pedestrians and vehicles to pass. This stop must be made before crossing the sidewalk area. Failure to stop is against the law.
